transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 14:32 (PDT)
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Derek Huang (Redwood SE), Karen Lowe (Elm Street - Head of MLOps), Marcus Reed (Elm Street - CTO), Alice Park (Elm Street - Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Elm Street's infra constraints and requirements for dedicated GPU capacity. Focus on isolation (VPC/on-prem), burst strategy for peaks, scaling expectations, and security/compliance gating. Agreement to run a pilot benchmark and share SOC2/docs.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Isolation and data residency
- Burst and autoscale behavior for dedicated pools
- Performance expectations (p99 latency, throughput)
- Security + compliance (KMS/HSM, SSO, audit logs)

Action items (short):
- Redwood to send pricing and SKUs, security packet, and benchmark plan
- Elm Street to share sample workload and security questionnaire

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we can kick off, quick intros?
[00:08] Marcus (Elm Street): yeah Marcus here, CTO, we've got Karen and Alice as well. thanks Sofia.
[00:12] Karen (Elm Street): hi all, Karen, focusing on ops and ml infra.
[00:15] Alice (Elm Street): Alice, security.
[00:18] Derek (Redwood): hey team, Derek here, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll run through the technical parts and benchmarks later.

[02:05] Sofia (Redwood): high level, Elm Street is evaluating dedicated capacity vs hosted. can you tell us current traffic and why dedicated is on the table?
[02:20] Marcus (Elm Street): sure, so we're a hedge fund-ish firm, uh lots of internal models for research and some customer-facing analytics. peak gen is about 1200 concurrent requests for short prompts but usage is spiky - end of day re-runs, earnings windows, that sort of thing.
[02:45] Karen (Elm Street): right now we're on a mix of cloud VMs and managed llm endpoints, and cost is getting sticky, also we need stronger isolation for some regulated funds.

[04:10] Derek (Redwood): makes sense. typical dedicated discussion is reserved GPU pools - you get predictable throughput and data isolation. we support private VPC deployments too if you need. question: do you need air-gapped on-prem, or VPC with customer-managed networking?
[04:28] Alice (Elm Street): initially VPC with customer-managed subnets; on-prem might be later for the most sensitive funds. also we need KMS integration and HSM-backed keys for model access logs.
[04:42] Sofia (Redwood): got it, so KMS and HSM are must-haves; we do integrations with major KMS providers and have HSM options for private deployments.

[06:00] Marcus (Elm Street): how does Redwood handle burst capacity? some days we exceed baseline by 4x for a couple hours. we can't have long tail throttling during earnings windows.
[06:15] Derek (Redwood): two main levers: reserved base capacity plus burst pools. you can provision a baseline of GPUs and configure autoscale + burst policies. burst can be pre-provisioned reserved spare or ephemeral cloud burst depending on deployment mode. note: for Private (on-prem) burst is limited by physical capacity, for Dedicated we can configure reserved burst nodes in the same account/region.
[06:46] Karen (Elm Street): is burst instant? we care about p99 latency staying under 500ms for short prompts.
[06:55] Derek (Redwood): bursts are quick, typically tens of seconds to a couple minutes to ramp depending on cold start and model warm caches. we also do continuous batching and KV prefix caching to reduce cold token costs; so for many short prompt workloads you see effective latency improvements even during bursts.

[09:10] Marcus (Elm Street): hmm tens of seconds could be problematic for some trading signals. can we do a mixed strategy: keep hot pool sized for p99 critical paths and use burst for non-critical batch jobs?
[09:25] Sofia (Redwood): yes that's a common pattern - hot pool for latency-sensitive routes, separate batch pool for heavy throughput tasks. we can also route by policy so critical requests always hit the hot pool.

[11:00] Alice (Elm Street): on the security side, we need audit logs, token-level tracing, RBAC, and SSO integration. do you expose logs to our SIEM?
[11:15] Derek (Redwood): we have token-level cost/latency breakdowns in the console and an exportable audit log that can stream to customer SIEMs (via S3, Kafka, or direct syslog). SSO/SAML via IdP supported and role bindings for RBAC.

[13:30] Karen (Elm Street): compliance: SOC 2 is critical, also we do periodic third-party pen-tests - do you support customer-supplied pen-test windows for Dedicated?
[13:45] Sofia (Redwood): yes, Dedicated customers can schedule pen-tests; for Private/on-prem we coordinate with the infra team. we'll share our SOC 2 report and our standard pen-test process.

[15:10] Marcus (Elm Street): how do you handle model variants and fallbacks? if our primary model is down or overloaded we need graceful degradation to a smaller model, not total failures.
[15:28] Derek (Redwood): smart routing handles that - you can pin model versions, set fallback policies (downgrade to quantized variant or lower-accuracy model), or route to another region or capacity tier. rollouts can be canaryed too.

[17:50] Karen (Elm Street): pricing - is Dedicated per-GPU monthly + overage? we need predictable costs for budgeting.
[18:00] Sofia (Redwood): typically reserved monthly commit for a set of GPU SKUs, plus burst/overage options. we'll send a pricing sheet but common patterns are monthly reserved nodes for baseline and a discounted burst or hourly overage model.

[20:10] Marcus (Elm Street): ok, what about latency numbers - can you share p50/p95/p99 for common models at our token lengths?
[20:25] Derek (Redwood): we can - but we'll need sample workloads; we'll also run benchs on our Dedicated pool with similar token length distribution. we suggest a pilot: 2-4 week benchmark, run your sample prompts, capture latency and token cost.

[23:00] Alice (Elm Street): for encryption, we need customer-managed keys and HSM; logs must not expose raw PII and must be retained based on our retention policy. can we set retention and redaction rules?
[23:20] Derek (Redwood): yes, log retention and redaction rules configurable; we support customer-managed KMS keys and HSM-backed key wrapping for certain private deployments. we'll include details in the security packet.

[25:40] Karen (Elm Street): integration: we have a Kubernetes infra, do you provide a private control plane or do we run the runtime?
[25:55] Derek (Redwood): two options: Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane with our runtime deployed into your VPC; for on-prem we provide the package and orchestration recipes. Dedicated (hosted) is fully managed but with VPC peering and network isolation options. we'll map pros/cons in the follow-up doc.

[28:10] Sofia (Redwood): timeline and stakeholders? when are you looking to pilot?
[28:20] Marcus (Elm Street): we'd like a pilot within 4-6 weeks, with procurement and security sign-off to follow if the pilot meets latency and isolation requirements. stakeholders: me and Karen, plus procurement and the security team (Alice).

[30:00] Karen (Elm Street): success criteria: p99 < 500ms on latency-sensitive routes, predictable monthly spend within 10%, and SOC2 + KMS compliance.

[31:15] Derek (Redwood): noted. for pilot sizing I'd recommend starting with a 4-GPU hot pool for latency-critical and a 16-GPU burst-capable pool for batch and spiky loads, but we'll calibrate after we see sample QPS and token lengths.

[33:40] Marcus (Elm Street): can you guarantee isolation - tenant isolation, no noisy neighbor? we need strong guarantees for fund-level isolation.
[33:55] Sofia (Redwood): Dedicated means reserved GPUs for your account; no multi-tenant sharing on those nodes. we can also enable strict network policies and separate storage. for the highest bar, Private on-prem gives total infra control.

[36:00] Alice (Elm Street): one last question on data residency - some funds require EU-only residency. can Dedicated be region pinned?
[36:12] Derek (Redwood): yes you can pin capacity to region, and we support geo-fencing for data residency. we'll call out region availability in pricing.

[38:30] Karen (Elm Street): ok next steps?
[38:35] Sofia (Redwood): we'll do: 1) send pricing and SKU options, 2) security packet (SOC2, pen-test policies, KMS/HSM details), 3) benchmark plan and sample spreadsheet, 4) propose pilot dates.
[38:50] Marcus (Elm Street): we'll compile sample prompts and send the security questionnaire - Alice will own that.

[39:15] Alice (Elm Street): yup I'll send questionnaire and a list of our compliance constraints by EOD Tuesday.

[40:00] Derek (Redwood): i'll draft the benchmark plan and sample spreadsheet and share by Friday. Sofia will include the pricing.

[41:20] Sofia (Redwood): perfect. any blockers?
[41:25] Karen (Elm Street): procurement will want contract terms - SLA, uptime, data handling. we'll need that for procurement review.
[41:40] Sofia (Redwood): noted - we'll include SLA language and bring legal on the follow-up if needed.

[43:00] Marcus (Elm Street): sounds good. final note - latency for trading signals is really critical so we'll prioritize the hot pool and routing policies in the pilot.
[43:15] Derek (Redwood): yes we'll include a hot-path test in the benchmark.

[45:00] Sofia (Redwood): recap and owners: Sofia sends pricing + security packet (due 2026-03-06), Derek shares benchmark plan (due 2026-03-08), Alice sends security questionnaire (due 2026-03-07). schedule deep dive for benchmarks after docs are exchanged.
[45:25] Marcus (Elm Street): ok thanks all.
[45:30] Karen (Elm Street): thanks.
[45:32] Alice (Elm Street): thanks, bye.
[45:40] Sofia (Redwood): bye everyone.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings on product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate"), speaker overlap near the end, some filler words left in for authenticity.
